answer: Here is one mechanism that works: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because lotus only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, yarrow is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any ridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
